title: What rehat means
hookLine: rehat is the Sikh code of living, how the teaching becomes daily life

cards: Before light, in a Sikh home, someone is already up. Washed, hair combed, a prayer said from memory in the half-dark.
Later there's work, a meal shared with whoever is at the table, a prayer at evening and another before sleep. Ask which rule makes all that happen and the answer isn't one rule.
It's a word for the whole shape of a day lived by the teaching: rehat.

teach.b: The word is usually linked to the Punjabi rehna, to live, to stay, to dwell. So rehat is, at heart, a way of living: for Sikhs, the discipline that turns the Gurus' teaching into daily habit.
Today the shared written reference is the Sikh Rehat Maryada, a short code agreed by Sikh leaders and scholars, which you'll look at closely in a few days. It holds much more than rules.
It begins with who a Sikh is: someone who believes in one God, the ten Gurus, the Guru Granth Sahib and the Gurus' teaching.
Then the day: rising early, bathing, remembering the Name, reciting the set daily prayers, the nitnem, in the morning, the evening and before sleep.

teach.h: THE DAY, THE WORK, THE SANGAT.
teach.b: Then honest work, sharing, and serving others. Then life together: the gurdwara, the langar, the rites of birth, marriage and death.
And for those who take amrit, the five Ks and a few things to avoid, which come over the next days. Here's the key.
Rehat isn't meant as a checklist to earn God's favor; the Gurus were blunt that empty ritual saves no one.

teach.h: NOT A CHECKLIST: A LIVED SHAPE.
teach.b: It's the shape a life takes when the teaching is actually lived: truth lived, from a couple of weeks ago. Sikhs also keep the rehat in very different degrees, and that's discussed honestly within the community.

how: The Sikh Rehat Maryada, published by the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee, describes daily prayers (nitnem) in the morning, evening and at night, honest work, sharing and service; how closely each Sikh keeps it varies.

games.q: someone asks you what the Sikh rehat is. what's the best short answer from today?
o: a list of rules to earn God's favor.
a way of living: the day, the work and the community, shaped by the Gurus' teaching.
a set of rules only for priests.
games.why: rehat begins with who a Sikh is and moves through the day, honest work, sharing and the sangat: a way, not a list.

practice: Think of one thing you always do, or never do, because of what you care about: maybe you don't lie to your kids, or you always call your mother, or you never eat in front of someone hungry.
Put it into one short sentence, a rule you live by, and rest with the breath while you hold it.

wordCard.voice: Rehat. The Sikh way of living, from rehna, to live: the discipline that turns the Gurus' teaching into the shape of a day.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: rehat, the way of living; from rehna, to live, to dwell.

carryVoice: Your line: a way, not a list. It starts before light and ends after dark. Day two hundred sixty-four, done.
